sanskrit_verse:
वैश्यस्य क्षत्रियाक्रोशे दण्डनीयः प्रदो भवेत् ।
तदर्धं क्षत्रियो वैश्यं क्षिपन् विनयमर्हति ॥
transliteration: vaiśyasya kṣatriyākrośe daṇḍanīyaḥ prado bhavet | tadardhaṃ kṣatriyo vaiśyaṃ kṣipan vinayam arhati ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When a Vaishya abuses a Kshatriya, the prescribed restitution is to be given; when a Kshatriya insults a Vaishya, he deserves only half that penalty.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is determined by varna-dharma alignment
Causation arises from violation of svadharma
Capacity-based responsibility reflects spiritual-social role integrity
Restoration logic aligns consequence with hierarchical dharma disruption
Consciousness alignment requires proportional response rooted in Varna-svabhava
executable_legal_axioms: IF actor = Vaishya AND target = Kshatriya AND abuse = true THEN restitution = full measure
IF actor = Kshatriya AND target = Vaishya AND insult = true THEN restitution = half measure
IF actor.varna_dharma_integrity < target.varna_dharma_integrity THEN consequence_proportion = reduced
ALL consequences MUST map to consciousness_realignment NOT punitive_suffering
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this principle establishes varna-specific thresholds for responsibility and restitution. The court must assess not just action but also the dharmic positioning of both parties. Disruption of higher-dharma roles invokes greater consequence; thus, Vaishya-to-Kshatriya disrespect incurs full restitution while Kshatriya-to-Vaishya incurs half, reflecting inherent social-karmic hierarchy and capacity.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramana-based causality shows that varna-specific actions disrupt sequential social harmony (anupurvasah). Responsibility is proportional to one's svadharma position. Consequence is not punitive but restorative—designed to realign consciousness and restore energetic-social balance without inflicting suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Offender performs corrective ritual aligned with varna-dharma
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Public acknowledgment of dharma misalignment
Capacity Restoration: Guided practice to strengthen svadharma awareness
Integrity Reintegration: Mediated reconciliation between varnas based on dharma roles
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority. Dharma is restored through consciousness-aligned restitution. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
